_comment: Technical Design v0.38–v0.39's Setting Pack and Player Interface: the player's words. Command names and hints, refusal reasons, example lines, and every label the player screen shows. Code fills the {named} placeholders and writes none of these words itself (CC-20261111-08, #61; the screen's labels CC-20261111-09, #62).

commands._comment: Keyed by the game's action. `name` is what the player types; `usage` shows its arguments; `hint` is the command menu's one line.

bribe.name: /bribe
bribe.hint: Hand the guest you're alone with n {currency}.

repay.name: /repay
repay.hint: Renounce one French pension, your own or a relative's, for {amount} {currency}.

conclude.name: /conclude
conclude.hint: Note privately what you've worked out. Only your latest counts.

refusals._comment: Sent to the player alone, with the reason. Mechanics' reasons: mistimed, not allowed, can't afford it, unknown guest, not present.
refusals.cant_afford: You can't afford that: you have {purse} {currency}.
refusals.not_positive: Name a number of {currency} above nothing.
refusals.message_used: You've spoken your piece this turn. You can speak again next turn.
refusals.message_held: Your words are waiting to be spoken.
refusals.pension_refused: You hold no pension you could renounce for {holder}, or can't pay it back.
refusals.end_mistimed: There's no private conversation for you to end.

acts._comment: Midnight: why the acts were refused (Mechanics, Murder Round).
acts.count: Choose exactly the number of acts you may take tonight.
acts.self: You can't take an act on yourself.
acts.same_guest: Each of your acts must name a different guest.

examples: I hear the Signoria meets early tomorrow.
You seem very sure of that. Who told you?
My family has long memories, and longer purses.
I'd rather speak of this somewhere quieter.
orientation: Speak as your character would, plainly. The other guests react to strange talk as guests would.

screen._comment: The player screen's labels (TD v0.39, The screen).
screen.title: Gonfaloniere

input.placeholder: Say something. @ addresses a guest; / opens the commands.
input.used: You've spoken your piece this turn.
input.held: Your words will be spoken at the next pause.
input.waiting: The company waits for you: speak, or pass.
input.answering: {name} has addressed you: answer, or pass.
input.closing: {name} has ended the conversation: a last word, or pass.

seat.inviteeTitle: The conversation with {initiator} is over. Where do you go?
seat.loneTitle: You're left alone. Join a group.

midnight.title: Midnight
midnight.introTwo: Choose one or two acts for tonight.

death.you: You have died. From here you watch, as the city does.

end.title: The evening is over
end.dead: You did not survive the night.
